newsitem.title: INDIA: India rolls out historic engine for tourists.
newsitem.headline: India rolls out historic engine for tourists.

text.p: India's railway ministry has pulled out of mothballs a steam engine, used by British troops to crush a national rebellion 140 years ago, to pull tourists, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Friday.
The agency said the 1855 British-built "Fairy Queen" would run between New Delhi and Alwar, in the state of Rajasthan known for its legendary maharajahs, from February next year.
India boasts one of the world's largest railway networks but has replaced most of its steam locomotives with diesel and electric versions.

Steam locomotives played a major role in what Indians regard as their first war of independence from British rule in 1857, when the smoke-belching machines were viewed with suspicion as carriers of evil spirits to enslave local people.
The Fairy Queen had been based at the Delhi-based national Rail Musuem, along with dozens of other aged engines, for many decades.
PTI said the Fairy Queen would carry only one 60-seater carriage, with a pantry car.
A $500 return fare to Alwar, 150 km (94 miles) from New Delhi, will include an overnight visit to the nearby Siriska Tiger sanctuary, it said.
When operational, it is believed the engine will be the oldest railway engine on active duty in the world, PTI said.
